pages.title: 1. The Valkyrien Era
pages.text: Following the rapid development of Valkyrien technology, space travel and colonization entered a new age. The Interstellar Exploration Guild's most ambitious undertaking was Project Eden AeroSpace (EAS). It mass-produced the Eden-class light exploration vessel—primitive by modern standards in control, propulsion, and weaponry—and sent explorers on random trajectories to find habitable worlds and record coordinates for later settlement. The project greatly expanded the known galaxy, but even after four upgrades the Eden class suffered an alarming loss rate from crashes, disappearances, and localized physics thread crashes (PTCs): irreversible events that permanently froze every ship in an area. Project Eden soon faced severe difficulties.

pages.title: 2. A New Control System
pages.text: While upgrading the Eden class for greater stability, the Guild's research division also pursued fundamentally new technologies. Valkyrien technology, however, depended on the extremely unstable and dangerous antigravity substance known as Wanderlite. In the early days, even mining raw ore could trigger small PTCs. Despite later advances in extraction and refining, Wanderlite retained the highest spacetime hazard classification. Performance improvements reached a dead end, and several catastrophic, wide-area PTCs followed. The Guild settled for developing a new control system designed to avoid PTCs wherever possible: vsie, the predecessor of AeroIE.

pages.title: 3. An Ancient Technology Returns
pages.text: The damage caused by large-scale PTCs forced the Guild to suspend Project Eden until vsie was complete. Just as its research neared completion, an ancient technology suddenly returned to public attention: Aeronautics. Built by combining the venerable Create technology with long-overlooked End Stone, it resembled Valkyrien technology in ship assembly and physics, but was vastly more stable. A few dozen Valkyrien ships in proximity could produce the heavy freezing that preceded a PTC, while hundreds of Aeronautics vessels could safely make contact.

pages.title: 4. Aeronautics, Integrated
pages.text: Create technology has a long history, and the rediscovery of Aeronautics was essentially an archaeological achievement. As the public marveled at enormous ancient airships and warships—and wondered why the technology had vanished for so long—the Guild recognized that its unfinished vsie control system could be ported to Aeronautics. It immediately abandoned the Valkyrien prototype, redirected all development toward Aeronautics, and ultimately released AeroIE.

pages.title: 5. New Prospects and Challenges
pages.text: Although the first AeroIE release contained relatively little, it changed the perception of Aeronautics from "a toy for recreating ancient machines" into "practical interstellar exploration technology." A new generation of vessels built with Aeronautics and AeroIE soon became the backbone of exploration and expansion thanks to their exceptional stability and reliability.

Yet opportunity brought competing interests. The former Interstellar Exploration Guild continued its expeditions and colonization under the name Project Eden (EAS), but gradually lost its cooperative character. It became an interstellar megacorporation dominated by the division that controlled AeroIE—and no one knows what consequences that may bring...
